delivery.description: The delivery ULID. Matches X-Tmesis-Delivery. Duplicated in the body so a receiver that logs bodies has the dedupe key without the headers.

occurred_at.description: RFC3339 UTC, when the event happened on the node. ORDER BY THIS, never by arrival: delivery is unordered.

session.description: The publish session whose bucket output was fenced. Empty for a crash-recovery seal, which belongs to no running session.

prefix.description: The stream's object key root under the live destination, e.g. live/show-2041-main: the unit a single writer owns.

cause.description: CLOSED set. superseded is a higher fencing epoch, the normal takeover; released, holder_changed and missing mean the grant disappeared with no higher epoch, and are always an incident.

held_epoch.description: The FENCING epoch this node wrote under. Not the session epoch and not the key epoch.

observed_epoch.description: The highest fencing epoch on record for this prefix when the fence was detected. Higher than held_epoch when cause is superseded, equal to it otherwise.

new_holder.description: The holder of the grant of record, or null when the prefix is released or unheld. On one box this is usually this node's own name: a takeover fences its own predecessor.

writes_stopped_at.description: RFC3339 UTC, when this node stopped writing the prefix. Before occurred_at: the node stops first and tells afterwards. Up to the live destination's upload_concurrency objects already in flight may still land after it; closing that needs conditional writes, which arrive with FLEET.

abandoned_uploads.description: Objects this grant still owed when it stopped. They stay in the node's ledger at held_epoch and are reconciled by the next holder or the next start: segments are uploaded, playlists and init segments are retired, never uploaded over the current holder's.
